title: Execution Sequence Optimization for Processing In-Memory using Parallel Data Preparation
problem: State-of-the-art PIM synthesis algorithms prepare output memory cells greedily immediately after cells expire, causing sequential column preparation instead of leveraging parallel data preparation instructions. This inefficiency limits energy and performance gains in MAGIC-based PIM systems.
motivation: PIM promises unprecedented computing capabilities for high-data-rate applications, but optimizing memory cell preparation sequences is critical to achieving energy and latency improvements.
method: The PREP framework postpones data preparation instructions until all prepared cells are consumed, then executes accumulated memory cell preparations in parallel to free memory for functional evaluations. It explores a frontier of area-performance solutions using execution sequence optimization.
key_novelty: Deferring data preparation instructions to enable parallel batch preparation of memory columns rather than greedy sequential preparation.
contributions: PREP framework for execution sequence optimization in PIM systems with MAGIC logic style
Postponement-based scheduling to accumulate and parallelize memory cell preparation
27% energy consumption and 25% latency reduction versus state-of-the-art synthesis tools
Area-performance trade-off exploration with neutral crossbar memory cost
primary_theme: Parallel data preparation scheduling in PIM systems
